events_chronological: A virus let loose in the last years of the century kills most of the human race and drives the survivors below ground.
Decades on, the scientists running the underground colony send convicts up to gather specimens, and one of them volunteers.
He is sent back through time, arrives six years too early, and is arrested raving about a plague.
In the asylum a psychiatrist interviews him, and he meets the son of a celebrated virologist.
He is hauled back to the future and questioned about a recorded message the scientists have recovered.
He is sent to the right year and abducts the psychiatrist, who has since written a book about apocalyptic prophecy.
The two of them find graffiti for a shadowy group and trace the virologist's son to his father's estate.
The son denies everything and says the idea of stealing the virus was the convict's own, from the asylum.
The psychiatrist comes across a photograph from the first great war of a soldier who is unmistakably him.
He decides he has been mad all along and asks to be allowed to stay where he is.
She finds a bullet fired in the first great war in an X-ray of him and realises he has been telling the truth.
The shadowy group turn out to be animal rights activists who free the zoo animals and shut the virologist in a cupboard.
The pair go to the airport in disguise to stop the virologist's assistant, who is the real carrier.
She spots the carrier, he runs at the man with a gun, and airport police shoot him dead while a small boy watches from the concourse.
The carrier passes through the gate with the virus in his luggage, taking the next seat to one of the scientists sent back from the future.
nonlinear_category_reason: Thirteen of fourteen scenes run forward; the exception is the shooting at the airport, shown in fragments from the opening as a recurring dream and only placed at the very end.
syuzhet_notes: The telling opens on a fragment of the airport shooting and keeps returning to it as a dream, without the audience or the protagonist being able to place it. Only in the closing minutes is it shown whole and revealed as his own death, watched by his childhood self.
fabula_notes: The dream and the ending are one event, counted once here at its chronological position near the end. Everything else runs forward, including the jumps between the two periods, which follow the protagonist's own sequence.
